name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q01 - Origin of non-biodegradable pollutants

questiontext.text: Non-biodegradable pollutants are created by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollutants are broadly classified into biodegradable and non-biodegradable based on whether natural decomposers (such as bacteria and fungi) can break them down into harmless simpler substances.

Step 2: Evaluation
Natural processes and disasters generally release biodegradable materials or naturally cycling substances. In contrast, synthetic and persistent materials such as plastics, glass, synthetic pesticides (like DDT), and heavy-metal-containing industrial wastes are manufactured or concentrated through human activities and resist microbial decomposition.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Non-biodegradable pollutants are created by humans.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q02 - Harmful particulate matter diameter CPCB

questiontext.text: According to the Central Pollution Control Board, the diameter of particles that are responsible for causing great harm to human health is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Particulate matter (PM) in air pollution varies in size, and smaller particles penetrate deeper into the human respiratory tract.

Step 2: Evaluation
According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), particulate size \(2.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}\) or less in diameter (\(\text{PM}_{2.5}\)) is responsible for causing the greatest harm to human health. These fine particulates can be inhaled deep into the lungs, causing breathing and respiratory symptoms, irritation, inflammation, lung damage, and premature death.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The diameter of particles responsible for causing great harm to human health is 2.5 micrometer.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q03 - Material used for sound proofing rooms

questiontext.text: The material generally used for sound proofing of rooms like a recording studio and auditorium is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Soundproofing involves using porous or lightweight acoustic-absorbing materials that trap sound waves and reduce reverberation and noise transmission.

Step 2: Evaluation
Styrofoam (expanded polystyrene) is a lightweight, porous, closed-cell foam widely used as an acoustic insulator in recording studios, auditoriums, and similar spaces to absorb sound energy and prevent echo. Cotton, coir, and solid wood are not the standard primary material used for commercial acoustic soundproofing panels in this context.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The material generally used for sound proofing of rooms like a recording studio and auditorium is styrofoam.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q04 - Main constituent of Compressed Natural Gas

questiontext.text: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is a clean-burning gaseous fuel used in automobiles to reduce vehicular air pollution.

Step 2: Evaluation
Natural gas consists primarily of methane (\(\text{CH}_4\)), typically around 85–95%, compressed to less than 1% of its volume at standard atmospheric pressure. Propane and butane are the main components of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), not CNG.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is methane.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q05 - Most problematic aquatic weed

questiontext.text: World's most problematic aquatic weed is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Invasive aquatic weeds multiply rapidly in nutrient-rich (eutrophic) water bodies, choking waterways and depleting dissolved oxygen.

Step 2: Evaluation
Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) is an exotic free-floating aquatic plant introduced into India for its mauve-coloured flowers. It grows at an alarming rate, covers entire water surfaces, blocks sunlight, drains oxygen from water, and leads to the death of aquatic organisms, earning it the name "Terror of Bengal" and making it the world's most problematic aquatic weed. Azolla (a water fern used as biofertiliser), Wolffia (a tiny duckweed), and Trapa (water chestnut) do not cause comparable ecological devastation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The world's most problematic aquatic weed is Eichhornia.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q06 - Pollutants exhibiting biomagnification

questiontext.text: Which of the following exhibits biomagnification?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biomagnification refers to the progressive increase in the concentration of a persistent, non-biodegradable toxic substance at successive trophic levels in a food chain.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because organisms cannot metabolise or excrete substances like mercury and DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane), these toxins accumulate in body tissues and become increasingly concentrated from producers to primary consumers, secondary consumers, and top predators. In contrast, sulphur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) is a gaseous air pollutant that does not biomagnify through food chains.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both mercury and DDT exhibit biomagnification.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q07 - Expanded chemical name of DDT

questiontext.text: The expanded form of DDT is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
DDT is a synthetic organochlorine insecticide well known for environmental persistence and biomagnification in aquatic and terrestrial food chains.

Step 2: Evaluation
The abbreviation DDT stands for dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, a chlorinated hydrocarbon compound containing two chlorophenyl rings attached to a trichloroethane group.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The expanded form of DDT is dichloro diphenyl trichloroethane.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q08 - Material taking longest time for biodegradation

questiontext.text: Which of the following material takes the longest time for biodegradation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodegradation rate depends on the chemical composition and structural density of a material, as well as how easily microorganisms can enzymatically break it down.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cotton, paper, and jute are plant-derived cellulosic materials that are readily decomposed by soil microbes within weeks to a few months. Bone, however, consists of a dense mineralised matrix (calcium phosphate / hydroxyapatite) combined with collagen fibres, which resists rapid microbial breakdown and takes many years to decompose.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Bone takes the longest time for biodegradation among the listed materials.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q09 - Identifying incorrect statement on environmental concepts

questiontext.text: Choose the incorrect statement.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Evaluating environmental protocols, greenhouse gases, atmospheric measurement units, and waste disposal methods requires verifying each scientific fact.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty designed to control the emission of ozone-depleting substances (such as CFCs). Methane and carbon dioxide are major greenhouse gases responsible for global warming. Incinerators are crucial for the safe disposal of hazardous hospital wastes. However, Dobson units (DU) are used to measure the thickness of the ozone column in the atmosphere from the ground to the top of the atmosphere—not the oxygen content of air.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that Dobson units are used to measure oxygen content of air.

answer.text: The Montreal protocol is associated with the control of emission of ozone depleting substances
Methane and carbon dioxide are green house gases
Dobson units are used to measure oxygen content of air
Use of incinerators is crucial to disposal of hospital wastes

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q10 - Maximum indoor chemical pollution source

questiontext.text: Among the following which one causes maximum indoor chemical pollution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Indoor air pollution arises from combustion of fuels and release of volatile or particulate chemicals inside enclosed spaces.

Step 2: Evaluation
Coal is a solid fossil fuel that undergoes incomplete combustion indoors, releasing large amounts of toxic gases such as carbon monoxide (\(\text{CO}\)), carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\)), sulphur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)), nitrogen oxides, and particulate soot. Burning cooking gas (LPG) burns much more cleanly, while mosquito coils and room sprays release comparatively smaller quantities of chemical pollutants.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Burning coal causes the maximum indoor chemical pollution among the given choices.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q11 - Composition of green scum in freshwater

questiontext.text: The green scum seen in the fresh water bodies is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nutrient enrichment (eutrophication) in freshwater bodies promotes excessive growth of photosynthetic microorganisms, forming visible green surface scums known as algal blooms.

Step 2: Evaluation
Both blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) and green algae (chlorophyceae) thrive in nutrient-rich freshwater and contain chlorophyll pigments that impart a green colour to the surface scum. Red algae (rhodophyceae) are predominantly marine and do not form typical freshwater green scums.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The green scum seen in freshwater bodies is due to both blue-green algae and green algae.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q12 - Comfortable sound loudness threshold for humans

questiontext.text: The loudness of a sound that a person can withstand without discomfort is about

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sound intensity is measured in decibels (dB). Undesired high-level sound causes noise pollution and physiological discomfort.

Step 2: Evaluation
A sound level up to about 80 dB can generally be tolerated by humans without significant discomfort. Sound levels above 80 dB cause discomfort, and brief exposure to extremely high sound levels of 150 dB or more (such as from a jet plane or rocket take-off) may damage eardrums and permanently impair hearing.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The loudness of a sound that a person can withstand without discomfort is about 80 dB.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q13 - Major worldwide source of noise pollution

questiontext.text: The major source of noise pollution world wide is due to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Noise pollution refers to excessive, unwanted sound that disrupts human health and environmental balance.

Step 2: Evaluation
Globally, the transport system—including road traffic (automobiles, buses, trucks, horns), railways, and aircraft—is the single largest and most widespread contributor to ambient noise pollution, affecting urban and suburban populations continuously compared to localised industrial plants or office equipment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The major source of noise pollution worldwide is the transport system.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q14 - Indian environmental acts and enactment years

questiontext.text: Match the following environmental acts with their respective years of enactment or amendment:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Government of India enacted several key environmental laws to prevent and control pollution across water, air, and the broader environment.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in 1974 to safeguard water resources. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act came into force in 1981 to control air pollution. The Environment (Protection) Act was passed in 1986 as an umbrella legislation to protect and improve environmental quality. Subsequently, in 1987, the Air Act was amended to include noise as an air pollutant.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: Environment Protection Act — 1986; Air Prevention & Control of Pollution Act — 1981; Water Act — 1974; Amendment of Air Act to include noise as an air pollutant — 1987.

subquestion.text: Amendment of Air Act to include noise as an air pollutant

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q15 - Conversion of unburnt hydrocarbons by catalytic converters

questiontext.text: Catalytic converters are fitted into automobiles to reduce emission of harmful gases. Catalytic converters change unburnt hydrocarbons into:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Catalytic converters contain expensive metals such as platinum-palladium and rhodium as catalysts to convert poisonous exhaust gases into less harmful products.

Step 2: Evaluation
As exhaust passes through the catalytic converter, unburnt hydrocarbons are oxidised into carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\)) and water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)). Simultaneously, carbon monoxide is oxidised to carbon dioxide and nitric oxide is reduced to nitrogen gas.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Catalytic converters change unburnt hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide and water.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q16 - Purpose of removing sulphur from petroleum

questiontext.text: Why is it necessary to remove sulphur from petroleum products?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fossil fuels such as petrol and diesel naturally contain sulphur impurities that oxidise during combustion in automobile engines.

Step 2: Evaluation
When sulphur-containing fuel is burnt, sulphur reacts with oxygen to form sulphur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) in exhaust fumes. Sulphur dioxide is a major air pollutant that causes respiratory ailments and contributes to acid rain. Therefore, strict fuel-quality norms (such as Euro/Bharat Stage standards) mandate reducing sulphur content in petrol and diesel to minimise \(\text{SO}_2\) emissions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
It is necessary to remove sulphur from petroleum products to reduce the emission of sulphur dioxide in exhaust fumes.

answer.text: To reduce the emission of sulphur dioxide in exhaust fumes
To use sulphur removed from petroleum for commercial purposes
To increase the life span of engine silencers

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q17 - Easiest impurity to remove from wastewater

questiontext.text: Which one of the following impurities is easiest to remove from wastewater?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Domestic sewage and wastewater contain three main types of impurities: suspended solids, colloidal materials, and dissolved solids (along with microorganisms).

Step 2: Evaluation
Suspended solids such as sand, silt, and clay are relatively large and insoluble, so they can be easily separated by simple physical processes like sedimentation, filtration, and screening during primary treatment. In contrast, dissolved salts, colloids, and microscopic bacteria require advanced biological or chemical treatment processes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Suspended solids are the easiest impurities to remove from wastewater.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q18 - Disease not caused by water contamination

questiontext.text: Which one of the following diseases is not caused due to contamination of water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water-borne diseases are transmitted through ingestion of water contaminated with pathogens (via the faecal–oral route).

Step 2: Evaluation
Cholera (caused by Vibrio cholerae), typhoid (caused by Salmonella typhi), and jaundice (commonly associated with Hepatitis A or E) are transmitted through contaminated water and food. Hepatitis-B, however, is a viral infection transmitted primarily through infected blood, body fluids, sexual contact, or contaminated needles—not through water contamination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hepatitis-B is not caused due to contamination of water.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q19 - Nutrient causing nuisance aquatic plant growth

questiontext.text: Nuisance growth of aquatic plants and bloom-forming algae in natural waters is generally due to high concentrations of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cultural eutrophication is the accelerated ageing of water bodies caused by human-induced enrichment of limiting nutrients.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nitrates and phosphates (phosphorus) from agricultural runoff, detergents, and domestic sewage act as major plant nutrients. High concentrations of phosphorus overstimulate the growth of algae and aquatic weeds, leading to algal blooms and unsightly scum.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Nuisance growth of aquatic plants and bloom-forming algae is generally due to high concentrations of phosphorus.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q20 - Cause of distinct colour in algal blooms

questiontext.text: Algal blooms impart a distinct colour to water due to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Algal blooms consist of dense populations of planktonic (free-floating) algae near the surface of nutrient-enriched water bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation
Different groups of algae possess characteristic photosynthetic and accessory pigments (such as chlorophylls, phycobilins, and carotenoids). Because millions of algal cells accumulate in the upper layer of water, their intracellular pigments directly impart a distinct green, blue-green, or reddish colour to the water body.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Algal blooms impart a distinct colour to water due to their pigments.

answer.text: formation of coloured chemicals in water facilitated by physiological degradation of algae.
absorption of light by algal cell wall.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q21 - Environmental pollutants and their ecological effects

questiontext.text: Match the environmental agents with their associated effects or phenomena:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different environmental pollutants and radiation cause distinct biological and ecological impacts.

Step 2: Evaluation
Excessive exposure to UV-B radiation causes inflammation of the cornea, a condition called snow blindness. Biodegradable organic matter in sewage is decomposed by aerobic microbes, which increases the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of water. DDT is a persistent pesticide that undergoes biomagnification across trophic levels in food chains. Phosphates act as limiting nutrients that accelerate algal growth and cause eutrophication in lakes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: UV — Snow blindness; Biodegradable Organic matter — BOD; DDT — Biomagnification; Phosphates — Eutrophication.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_BIOLOGY_CH16_MCQ_Q22 - Chemical involved in Bhopal gas tragedy

questiontext.text: In the textbook you came across “Three Mile Island and Chernobyl disasters associated with accidental leakage of radioactive wastes.” In India we had Bhopal gas tragedy. It is associated with which of the following?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial chemical disasters occur when toxic intermediates or products escape into the surrounding atmosphere.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on the night of December 2–3, 1984, at the Union Carbide India Limited pesticide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. It was caused by the accidental leakage of toxic methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas, resulting in thousands of immediate deaths and long-term health effects.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The Bhopal gas tragedy is associated with Methyl Isocyanate.
